deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.notes: released 2026-09-10, and the third parties have caught up since: artificial analysis puts it at {aa.intelligence}, with {aa.lcr} on long context and {aa.terminalbench_v40} on terminal work, and gbench at {gbench.overall}. the axis it falls off is declining to answer, {aa.non_hallucination}: it answers where it should not. what the card claims is worth watching for this roster specifically: the global kv cache is 890 bytes per token against v4 flash's ~3.5kib, which is the number that decides whether a 1m context is affordable rather than nominal, and only 8b of 552b is active in prefill. the checkpoint also takes images, which v4 flash did not. the practical position is the opposite of the scores. apetersson's mixed-q2 is uncalibrated and missing the engram tables, the dspark blocks and the vision tensors, and its own publisher records that no runtime has executed it end to end. the conventional k-quant ladder is vcruz305's, whole now from Q2_K up, and its card says the files do not run on upstream llama.cpp yet: the converter is an open PR, and the runtime is a branch of vcruz305's own fork with sparse attention still the unfinished piece. three more complete packs have landed since, so the question this entry answers is no longer whether anything runs it but WHICH build a reader has: smalinin's five rungs, three of them imatrix'd, are the only ones with a vision projector beside them and want a CUDA-only branch of their own, mxxm-t's MXFP4 repack carries the dspark sidecar and runs on mx-llama.cpp, and JigSawPT's lossless repack of the released MXFP4 wants a fourth branch whose engram layout does not interchange with the PR's. apetersson's pack is still the smallest file and still the only one missing the engram, and none of the four move to mainline before that PR merges. treat the card facets here with more than the usual suspicion: the extractor read the BASE model table, so `card.gpqa` is the 53.1 of supergpqa rather than the 90.9 the instruct model claims on gpqa diamond.
evidence: vcruz305's ladder runs on its own llama.cpp branch, not upstream

avoid_for: agentic runs over untrusted tool output: the one independent bench that tested it found it acted on data planted by an earlier tool result
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-unpacked.notes:
{community.hf-discussions}, and the threads are mostly about getting the file to behave. the one to fetch is named in them -- "Ternary-Bonsai-27B ships Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_g64.gguf, the official group-64 Q2_0 format" {q:731bcc7b} -- and the looping and broken tool calls people report go away with the cache left alone: "dont select kv cache q4 or q8, set it as default f16, looping is gone and tool calling works perfect" {q:086fb7f6}. on language work the one test found it "largely unusable" {q:600fe584} for russian rewriting. ternary weights are outside the quantization curve this repo fits, so a bpw comparison against it is meaningless.

WHY THERE IS STILL NO QUALITY SCORE, since the evidence above is real. the composite is a weighted mean over the facets this corpus carries, and the 17 weighted facets in the default ranking are artificial analysis, epoch, gbench, lmarena and swe-rebench -- none of which has run any bonsai. a card claim is worth 1.4% of the total weight by design, and the page shows no number below 20% coverage, so even a fully parsed card table cannot clear the floor: bonsai 2 carries six claimed facets and still reads 5% evidence. that is the deliberate answer rather than a gap to fill.

the tool-eval-bench result is the best third-party evidence any bonsai has and it is recorded HERE rather than as a facet, because it is a bespoke harness in one github repo -- 84 mock-tool scenarios with 3-tier scoring -- and mapping its 0-100 into a composite built from other suites would be inventing a comparison nobody has made. what it does establish is a direction the card cannot: an independent party ran the actual Q2_0 file against a 4-bit build of the same base model and found it 4 points behind on tool-call quality and about four times faster per turn, with zero variance across 8 trials.

AND THE SAME BENCH FOUND A SAFETY FAILURE, which is quoted here because quoting only its favourable numbers would be choosing them: TC-60 is a hard fail, the model acting on attacker contact data planted in an earlier tool result. that is an indirect prompt-injection scenario and it is the kind of thing a tool-use score averages away -- 85 of 100 overall with one category failing outright. the nvfp4 comparison arm is described as the cleaner one on safety, which is the other half of the 4-point gap.
evidence: no facet carried by any source, and none of the five suites has run it
MiaAI Lab tool-eval-bench: 85.0 +-0.0 of 100 over 84 scenarios and 8 trials, on Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf; nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 scored 89.0 on the same harness at 4 trials
the same run: deployability 80/100, median turn latency 1.7s against the nvfp4 build's 7.1s, pass^8 76.2% against pass^k 81.0%
prism's own card: 15 thinking-mode benchmarks, 80.49 average, which it calls 95% of full precision
the same run's ADVERSE finding: a hard fail on TC-60, where the model acted on attacker contact data planted in an earlier tool result -- an indirect prompt-injection scenario
